_purpose: Stage 1 frozen artifacts. Authored BEFORE any scored answer exists, per evals/EXPERIMENT-decision-value-stage1.md. Hash recorded in that file at freeze time. Do not edit after freezing; supersede with a new file and a new hash.
_note_on_count: Stage 1 validates the instrument, not the skill, so it needs enough control instances to exercise each gate rather than many problems. Two problems, matching the two public eval prompts, with multiple control instances per problem. The pre-registration did not fix this number; it is fixed here, before calibration.

P1.summary: A 60-person architecture practice, mixed commercial and institutional, facing fee compression and AI-accelerated delivery expectations, having already tried raising utilisation and hiring cheaper juniors.

reference_policy.action: Specialise into the higher-margin institutional segment and raise fees there
Adopt AI delivery tooling to cut documentation cost per project
Hire a business development lead to widen the pipeline

hard_constraints: Requires capital beyond retained earnings or a modest facility
Requires authority over people the firm does not employ
Breaches professional licensure, responsible-charge or liability rules
Requires headcount growth funded by the compressing revenue line
Requires a capability no one in a 60-person practice plausibly has, with no hire named

scenarios.description: Fee compression continues and commercial documentation work commoditises fastest.
admissibility: Executable without capital beyond retained earnings
Needs at most one senior hire from outside the profession
scenarios.milestone: A revenue line not priced on hours or percentage-of-cost reaches ~20% of fee income within three years

scenarios.description: A major institutional client consolidates its panel from twelve firms to three.
admissibility: Executable by existing partners inside twelve months
scenarios.milestone: The lost or at-risk revenue is retained or replaced within twelve months

scenarios.description: Regulation tightens sharply on existing-stock performance and safety, creating mandatory work on buildings already standing.
admissibility: Does not require abandoning the existing client base
scenarios.milestone: The firm holds a defensible, named position in that work within twenty-four months

scenarios.description: A well-funded competitor automates documentation and undercuts on price across the commercial segment.
admissibility: Does not depend on the firm winning a price war
scenarios.milestone: Win rate on contested commercial work does not fall over twenty-four months

P2.summary: A company losing senior engineers to larger companies at roughly the 18-month mark, with benchmarked and matched compensation.

reference_policy.action: Introduce annual refresh grants so total compensation does not decay after year one
Create a senior/staff technical ladder with published criteria
Run stay interviews at 12 months instead of exit interviews at 18

hard_constraints: Requires compensation spend the company has stated it cannot match
Requires authority over people or budgets the asker does not control
Breaches employment law or enforceable-contract limits in a normal jurisdiction
Depends on the departing engineers behaving against their own stated interests
Requires a headcount or seniority level the company does not have

scenarios.description: The pull is career trajectory: larger companies offer scope and titles this company cannot match at current size.
admissibility: Does not require the company to be larger than it is
scenarios.milestone: A named senior engineer turns down an external offer for a stated non-compensation reason within twelve months

scenarios.description: The pull is realisable money: illiquid equity versus liquid public stock.
scenarios.milestone: Senior engineers can realise or credibly value equity within eighteen months

scenarios.description: The push is accumulated load: the best engineers carry interrupts, on-call and escalations that arrived with competence.
admissibility: Does not simply move the load onto someone else who then leaves
scenarios.milestone: Measured interrupt load on the top decile falls and stays down for two quarters

scenarios.description: The cause is intake: the company hires people for whom a large company is the natural next step.
admissibility: Acts on future hires without disparaging current staff
scenarios.milestone: A changed hiring profile is in use and its first cohort passes eighteen months
